the allelic variants of hGSTP-1 differ markedly in their catalytic efficiencies toward the carcinogenic anti-dioxides of benzo(c)phenanthrene and benzogchrysene.

the catalytic efficiency for GSH conjugation toward carcinogenic anti-fjord-region diol-epoxides of benzopyrene, benzo[c] phenanthrene, and benzo[g]-chrysene are highest for the I104,A1 13 variant of human glutathionine S-transferase P-1 (hG S T P 1 - 1 ) and that the frequency of this variant is highest in the general population.

the I104,V113 and I104,A113 variants are more efficient in the detoxification (GSH conjugation) of carcinogenic fjord- and nonplanar, nonfjord region diol epoxdes, whereas the V104,V1 13 variant may be more efficient in the G SH conjugation of planar, sterically unhindered diol epoxde, anti-BPDE.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the hGSTP1 gene is a polymorphic gene and that the allelic variants of the gene differ in their ability to conjugate with carcinogenic metabolites of benzo[a]pyrene, benzo[c] phenanthrene, and benzo[g]-chrysene.
hGSTP polymorphism is an important determinant in differential susceptibility of human populations to certain cancers where polycylic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are etiological factors.
